title: Catalina Labs technical digest
body:
Quick capture from kick-off with Catalina Labs (internal follow-up for SEs)

Date: 2025-11-17 call (30m)
Participants: Dr. Mira Valdez (Catalina, ML lead), Rajesh Iyer (platform), Avery Chen (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood solutions), Lena Ortiz (Redwood security)

Summary (one-liner): Catalina wants a private, VPC-hosted assistant for clinical triage docs — strict PHI boundaries, predictable 100 qps sustained (burst to 350), p95 latency <= 300ms for short queries (<=128 tokens), retention & auditability requirements.

Notes / context:
- Workload: triage question-answering + short summarization of encounter notes; average request 40–120 tokens, worst-case generation 800 tokens (rare). Mostly synchronous API calls from their web UI and mobile app.
- Traffic shape: steady-state 80–120 rps during business hours, spikes around shift changes and batch uploads. Peak concurrency target ~40–60 concurrent streams.
- Data sensitivity: full PHI allowed in private deploy but must stay in their VPC, no outbound copies. Catalina has HSM for keys and wants KMS integration (AWS KMS + custom HSM option).
- Compliance: need audit logs, per-request provenance (model version, prompt hash, route). They will request SOC2 + HIPAA language in contract.

Technical constraints they raised:
- On-prem-ish network: limited egress, NAT gateway throttles; prefer inbound-only control-plane connectivity.
- Hardware: internal infra team has access to 4x A100 equivalent nodes initially, potentially more later. They want guidance on fit/perf.
- Model preference: start with open Llama-like family (they mentioned wanting to avoid proprietary models), will consider quantized 4-bit variants to reduce cost.
- Tokenization differences: their clinical templates include lots of shorthand and special tokens (lab codes). Need tokenizer warm-up and prompt engineering to avoid hallucination.

Immediate technical risks/gotchas (observations):
1) KV cache priming: many triage flows reuse patient context prefixes — recommend prefix caching and sticky routing to keep KV local. If we rely on naive stateless routing p95 will blow up.
2) Cold-starts on private deployment: their autoscale windows may spin new nodes; need warmup strategies (preload model shards + sample prompts). Consider a tiny always-on pool to keep hot KV caches.
3) Egress & audit: audit logs can be large (full prompt + response). Need retention policy and compression — propose exporting structured diffs instead of raw blobs for most events, retain raw only for flagged incidents.
4) Quantization QA: 4-bit quantization shows minor degradation on clinical abbreviations — require a short eval set (50 clinical QA pairs) they will provide. Leave a rollback path to fp16 if regression detected.
5) Latency budget: p95 <= 300ms is aggressive for generation >128 tokens. We should define SLO tiers: interactive (<=128 tokens, 300ms p95), async summarization (<=800 tokens, 2s p95).

Preliminary architecture notes (what we think will work):
- Private deployment with inbound-only control plane + egress gateway for updates (customer-managed).
- Dedicated small pool (2 nodes) pinned to low-latency region for interactive queries, burstable pool for heavy summarizations. Use GPU-aware autoscaler with node warmup hooks.
- Use Redwood Optimize recommendations: batching window 15–25ms for interactive, KV-caching on prefixed patient context, caching policy TTL 10–30 minutes depending on patient sessions.
- Storage: encrypted S3 in their VPC for model artifacts, audit logs forwarded to their SIEM (Splunk). KMS/HSM for keys.

Immediate action items (owner, due):
- Samir: send Catalina a short eval harness and instructions for the 50-case clinical QA set (due 2025-11-21).
- Avery: produce an initial cost/throughput sketch mapping 4x A100 equivalent -> expected qps/latency for candidate models (due 2025-11-20).
- Lena: draft minimal KMS/HSM integration checklist and required IAM roles for private control plane (due 2025-11-22).
- Catalina (Mira): share sample clinical templates (de-identified if needed) + the 50-case eval set (target 2025-11-25).
- Engineering: prototype prefix KV warmup script for model start (spike: pre-seed top 50 patient prefixes) — internal ticket JIRA-SOL-129.

Open questions (to resolve on follow-up call):
- Traffic isolation: do they require tenant-level hardware separation or VPC isolation is sufficient? (affects Dedicated vs Private licensing)
- Backup of audit logs: retention duration and encryption-at-rest key ownership model (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed).
- Disaster recovery RTO/RPO targets for the private cluster — ask ops team for internal expectations.

Notes for demo/proof-of-concept:
- Show a two-path flow: interactive triage (live chat, p95 under target) + async summarization (background job, eventual consistency)
- Demonstrate KMS integration and proof that no payload leaves the VPC during inference (network trace).
- Include simple quality regressions dashboard fed from their 50-case eval set to show quantization effects.

Misc small bits:
- Token accounting: remind Catalina that certain clinical templates with repeated structured fields increase token count vs naive char count. Provide quick script to estimate cost per encounter.
- Logging verbosity: recommend sample rate 1.0 for first two weeks, then reduce to 0.1 after tuning.

Next steps / scheduling:
- Schedule technical deep-dive w/ Catalina infra (60m) — propose 2025-11-24 10:00 PT.
- Internal sync w/ runtime team to validate warmup approach — 2025-11-21 sync, Samir to coordinate.

Random notes / scratch ideas:
- Could consider a tiny on-device inference proxy for initial on-site post rooms to handle zero-egress requirement for sensitive triage (long-term).
- Precompile common prompts into compact templates and store prompt hashes; use structured outputs to make auditing easier.

——
This doc is a working capture. Will turn into a short POC plan and an internal architecture sketch once initial numbers from Avery + Samir are in.

Unresolved: need Catalina to confirm whether they will accept Llama-ish license and if they have procurement constraints for open models.

End of notes.
